newsitem.title: UK: Russia has agreement on former Soviet trade debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia has agreement on former Soviet trade debt.

text.p: The Russian Ministry of Finance has agreed in principle on the key terms of the restructuring of the uninsured trade indebtedness of the former Soviet Union, SBC Warburg said in a statement on Thursday.
"With this agreement, Russia has normalised its relations with all the main creditor groups of the former Soviet Union," deputy minister of finance Mikhail Kasyanov said in the statement.

The agreement has been reached with 12 national creditor groups, representing creditors located in Austria, Belgium, Britain, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Holland, Italy, Japan, Sweden and Switzerland.
The Russian government had previously established this as one of its main goals for 1996, together with regaining access to the international capital markets, the statement said.

"Both these goals have now been achieved," Kasyanov said, adding the government was very pleased by the market's excellent reception of Russia's $1.0 billion debut Eurobond issued in November this year.
He said the government would shortly announce its borrowing plans for 1997.
